# Vocabulary runtime-policy/v0

Kernel runtime policies, such as Tetragon: policies, probes, the hooks they attach to, selectors and the workloads they cover. Defined in docs/models/runtime-policy-model.md. The schema is published at its ID, `https://schemas.projections.githubnext.com/vocabularies/runtime-policy/v0.json`; it is generated from TypeBox
definitions into [`packages/schemas/schemas/vocabularies/runtime-policy/v0.json`](../../../packages/schemas/schemas/vocabularies/runtime-policy/v0.json).

An extraction follows this vocabulary when its `vocabularies` include it; its `schema` must be `architecture/v0`. The extraction schema applies this one to it.

## Typed data

The engine checks every typed field, and reports a violation at its path. Other `data` fields are open JSON.

### Entities

| Kind | Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | `data.namespace` | string or null |  | The namespace of a namespaced policy, empty when it comes from where the policy is applied; null for a cluster-wide policy. |
| `policy` | `data.mode` | string |  | `enforce` or `monitor`. |
| `policy` | `data.scope` | string |  | The workloads it applies to, in plain language. |
| `policy` | `data.nodes` | string |  | Where the agent loads it. |
| `policy` | `data.effect` | string |  | The strongest effect of its selectors. |
| `hook` | `data.hookType` | string |  | `kprobe`, `fentry`, `tracepoint`, `lsm`, `uprobe`, `usdt` or `loader`. |
| `hook` | `data.stability` | string |  | How stable the hook is across kernels, such as `stable` or `kernel-internal`. |
| `hook` | `data.category` | string |  | What the hook observes, such as `file` or `network`. |
| `selector` | `data.effect` | string |  | What happens when it matches, such as `enforce` or `observe`. |
| `selector` | `data.enforcement` | string |  | `active`, `elided` (in a `monitor` policy) or `none`. |
| `selector` | `data.ordinal` | number |  | Its position in its probe. |
| `subject` | `data.subjectKind` | string |  | `workloads` or `binary`. |
